Definition: from G3326 and the middle voice of G3199; to care afterwards, i.e. regret:--repent (self).
BiblicalUsage: The son who said no and then repented and went, Judas who repented himself and brought back the silver, and Paul who says he did repent of his sharp letter — this word is the afterthought that changes the deed. It is regret that turns into a different course, and it is not the same in every man who feels it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that Judas is the warning here: he felt the regret and returned the money, yet never turned back to Christ, while the son in the parable repented and went, and that going is what made his repentance real. Repentance that never turns the feet is only regret, and regret alone saved no one.
